newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Absa says plans $110 mln GDR offer.
newsitem.headline: Absa says plans $110 mln GDR offer.

text.p: Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd (Absa) said on Thursday it planned a $110 million global depository receipt offer to fund the refinancing and expansion of its international operations.
The offer, which also includes ordinary shares, will be lead by Merrill Lynch and has an over-allotment option of 15 percent of the offer size, Absa said.
"That's it for the time being. There's no way we're going to do a rights issue or further issues of tier-one capital in the near future," Absa group executive director Alwyn Noeth told Reuters.
Noeth said the offer was expected to close by mid-July.

He said some of the funds would be used to replace short-term loan capital with more "permanent" equity capital at Absa's Hamburg and New York units as well as supplementing the capital bases of the London and Asian operations.
Noeth said the over-allotment would be kept as stand-by funding for future acquisitions.
"It would represent a war chest for future use if we should make any futher acquisitions. At this point in time there is nothing concrete in the pipeline," he said.
